themes_detail.label: Construction Surge & Building Violations
themes_detail.summary: General Construction/Plumbing complaints spiked to 66 this past week—a 303% increase from the 16.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting either a major construction project, widespread code violations, or deteriorating building conditions across Borough Park/Kensington.
evidence: 66 General Construction/Plumbing complaints last week vs. 16.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
646 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days, including 139 new buildings and 338 alterations—unusually high activity
reporting_angles: Are multiple large-scale construction projects underway simultaneously, and are contractors failing to follow noise/safety protocols?
Interview DOB to understand whether complaint volume reflects legitimate violations or permitting backlog; cross-reference active ULURP (39th & New Utrecht) with permit filings

themes_detail.label: Illegal Postings & Street Signage Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Posting complaints jumped to 18 this past week—a 586% increase from the 2.6 weekly average—while Street Sign - Dangling complaints reached 7 three weeks ago (522% above baseline), signaling either systematic street maintenance neglect or a coordinated illegal advertising campaign in the district.
evidence: 18 Illegal Posting complaints last week vs. 2.6 weekly average (586% increase, z-score 3.51)
7 Street Sign - Dangling complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average (522% increase, z-score 5.58)
Both spikes indicate either enforcement gap or accelerating street disorder
reporting_angles: Are illegal postings concentrated in a specific neighborhood corridor or tied to a particular type of advertisement (political, commercial, spam)?
Investigate whether DSNY/DOT street maintenance crew capacity is adequate, or whether illegal postering reflects organized activity

themes_detail.label: Building/Use Code Violations Exploding
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked dramatically 2 weeks ago to 66—an 826% increase from the 7.1 weekly average with z-score 11.52 (highest statistical severity)—suggesting potential illegal conversions, zoning violations, or unlicensed commercial activity spiking across the district.
evidence: 66 Building/Use complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 7.1 weekly average (826% spike, z-score 11.52—highest severity)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago but still the most statistically anomalous complaint category in dataset
Community board has repeatedly requested additional building inspectors (unsolved recurring request), suggesting existing capacity inadequate
reporting_angles: Obtain DOB inspection records for this district over past month; identify clusters of violations and complaint types (illegal residential conversions, basement apartments, unlicensed commercial use)
Interview building inspectors about staffing constraints; cross-reference recent permit filings (646 total) to assess whether violations reflect permitting backlog or rogue activity

themes_detail.label: Dumpster & Waste Management Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints spiked to 4 two weeks ago—a 700% increase from the 0.5 weekly average—while Vendor Enforcement complaints reached 7 last week (409% above baseline), suggesting emerging sanitation and street-vendor enforcement issues.
evidence: 4 Dumpster Complaint 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 4.95)
7 Vendor Enforcement complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average (409% increase, z-score 3.57)
Combined signal suggests waste management and street vending enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Survey local residents and businesses about overflowing dumpsters, illegal dumping, or waste collection delays
Investigate whether city has reduced DSNY service frequency or whether contractor compliance has deteriorated

themes_detail.label: Electrical & Infrastructure Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints reached 4 three weeks ago—a 540% increase from the 0.6 weekly average—raising safety concerns about downed wires, exposed electrical infrastructure, or deteriorating utility conditions affecting residents.
evidence: 4 Electrical complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% increase, z-score 4.85)
Timing is older than other spikes but still statistically severe and safety-critical
Community board has requested DEP capital funding (repeated budget request), suggesting aging utility infrastructure
reporting_angles: Contact Con Edison to determine whether Electrical complaints reflect streetlight outages, downed lines, or building-level violations
Assess whether this spike is isolated or part of broader aging-infrastructure pattern
